rules.ask: The level of this log call ($LEVEL) misstates the severity of what the surrounding code is handling at that point.
rules.note: Judge the level against the code path the call sits on, not against words in the message. A logger call whose first argument is not a message for a human is not a violation.
rules.subject: enclosing

rules.ask: This message ($MSG), shown to the user, tells them something other than what the surrounding code actually did.
rules.note: Judge only what the enclosing function shows. A message about what a server, a job or another system will do later is not checkable here and is not a violation. A call whose argument is not a message for a human, such as a body, a buffer or an empty string, is not a violation.
rules.subject: enclosing

rules.ask: This message ($MSG) describes a different condition from the one the check ($COND) actually tests.
rules.note: The check fires when the guard is true for if-throw shapes and when the condition is false for assert and invariant shapes; judge the message against the case in which it is shown. Only the condition and the message are compared; whether the check itself is correct is not the question.
